trace.notes: Resolved the supplied URL to a readable HTML Wikipedia category page titled 'Category:Unsolved problems in number theory'. The visible structure consists of category metadata, one subcategory block, and alphabetical lists of linked article titles rather than self-contained problem statements.

A recall-first scan found only linked topic titles such as 'Abc conjecture', 'Goldbach's conjecture', and 'Riemann hypothesis'. The page does not provide the technical statements needed to extract faithful standalone questions from the source itself.

Rejected the source for extraction because it is an index/category page rather than a technical source containing visible problem statements. Accepting article titles alone would violate the source adequacy and no-new-facts gates.
